speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your follow-up. I understand you are experiencing occasional shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after your tympanoplasty. To help me evaluate your recovery, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and if they are triggered by touching the ear or specific movements?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient's pain with eating and difficulty wearing earrings 12 weeks post-tympanoplasty raises concern for a recurrent or persistent cholesteatoma. Have you noticed any drainage from the ear, a foul odor, or any changes in the appearance of the ear canal or eardrum?

REQUEST IMAGES: Otoscopy_right_ear

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The pain triggered by eating suggests involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve or joint dysfunction, while the earring discomfort indicates canal issues. Have you noticed any fullness, clicking sounds, or restricted movement of your jaw when opening your mouth wide?

REQUEST IMAGES: Otoscopy_right_ear, Temporomandibular_Joint_XRay

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: History of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. Underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks prior. Social history: Works as a cashier at a local department store.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on your history of chronic ear infections and pain triggered by chewing, we need to rule out a recurrent cholesteatoma or TMJ dysfunction before considering nerve entrapment.

REQUEST TEST: High-resolution CT Temporal Bone (Right)
REQUEST IMAGES: Recent Audiogram, Otoscopy_Right_Ear
Do you have a history of jaw clicking, locking, or morning pain in your jaw joint?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No jaw clicking heard. No tenderness with palpation of the mandibular area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Based on the negative findings for TMJ dysfunction and your history of chronic ear infections and recent tympanoplasty, the pain triggered by eating suggests the involvement of the auriculotemporal nerve. Do you experience any tingling or numbness in your cheek, upper teeth, or scalp?

REQUEST TEST: High-resolution CT Temporal Bone (Right)
DIAGNOSIS READY: Auriculotemporal Nerve Entrapment
